marks.gloss_en: שנאמר: יען לא האמנתם בי -- had you believed, your time would not yet have come
הוא דאמר כי האי תנא -- R' Ami holds with R' Shimon b. Elazar, for whom even Moses and Aaron died through their sin (= p_r_ami_kerashbe)
even Moses and Aaron died through their sin
Yishai's death through the serpent's counsel is shown by Avigail's being called 'daughter of Nachash' though she was Yishai's daughter
four died through the serpent's counsel: Binyamin son of Jacob, Amram father of Moses, Yishai father of David, and Kilav son of David
מיתיבי: Moses and Aaron kept the whole Torah and died, and God answered 'one event to the righteous and the wicked' -- so there is death without sin
why did You penalise Adam with death? -- God: I commanded him an easy mitzva and he transgressed it

'Avigail daughter of Nachash' (II Sam 17:25) -- was she Nachash's daughter? she was Yishai's ('and their sisters Zeruiah and Avigail', I Chr 2:16); rather: the daughter of the one who died through the serpent's counsel
(entertained) the four-who-died baraita is the angels' tanna's
מקיש חפני לפנחס: מה פנחס לא חטא אף חפני לא חטא -- the verse juxtaposes Chofni to Pinchas; as Pinchas did not sin, so Chofni did not sin
אלא מה אני מקיים אשר ישכבון את הנשים -- the verse (I Sam 2:22) says they lay with the women
since they delayed the women's bird-offerings, so the women did not go to their husbands, Scripture credits them as if they lay with them (= p_yishkevun_shihu_kineihen)
how then do I uphold 'how they lay with the women'? since they delayed their bird-offerings so that they did not go to their husbands, Scripture credits them as if they lay with them
והלא כבר נאמר יכרת ה'... ומגיש מנחה -- אלא לאו שמע מינה פנחס לא חטא

'the Lord will cut off from the man who does this him that is awake and him that answers... and him that presents an offering' (Mal 2:12): if an Israelite, he will have none awake among the Sages nor answering among the disciples; if a priest, he will have no son who presents an offering
אלא הא כתיב אשר ישכבון -- 'they lay' is plural
ישכבן כתיב -- it is written [so as to read] yishkaven, singular
והכתיב אל בני כי לא טובה השמעה -- 'no, my sons' (I Sam 2:24) is plural
בני כתיב -- it is written [so as to read] beni, 'my son'
והכתיב מעברים -- 'you make [the people] transgress' is plural
מעבירם כתיב -- it is written maaviram
והכתיב בני בליעל -- 'the sons of Eli were scoundrels' (I Sam 2:12)
since Pinchas should have protested to Chofni and did not, Scripture credits him as if he sinned
whoever says the sons of Eli sinned is simply mistaken

as it is said: 'and Achiya son of Achituv, brother of Ichavod, son of Pinchas son of Eli, the Lord's priest' (I Sam 14:3) -- is it possible that sin came to his hand and Scripture traces lineage to him?
שנאמר: ויהיו בני יעקב שנים עשר -- stated right after the Bilhah incident, it teaches all twelve were equal, so Reuven had not sinned
Reuven did not sin -- whoever says he sinned is simply mistaken
אפשר עתיד זרעו לעמוד על הר עיבל ולומר ארור שכב עם אשת אביו, ויבא חטא זה לידו? -- his descendants would not curse the very sin of their ancestor
is it possible that his descendants would stand on Mount Eival and say 'cursed is he who lies with his father's wife' (Deut 27:20), and this sin came to his hand?
והיינו דכתיב: אז חללת יצועי עלה -- read yetzu'ai, 'my beds', plural: two beds
Acherim: he disturbed two beds, one of the Shechina and one of his father
[whether Reuven sinned] is as the tannaim [dispute over 'pachaz kamayim']
Rabban Gamliel: we still need the Modai['s exposition]
